title: List of Forms and Contact Details Required to Request Medical Records From UPMC in 2026
summary: A 2026 guide to UPMC medical record request forms, contact details, Pennsylvania fee limits, and authorization tips for personal injury law firms.
body_markdown:
UPMC operates[40+ hospitals](https://www.upmc.com/about/facts/numbers) and a large network of physician practices, and those locations don't all handle medical record requests the same way. Hospital records, physician-office records, and patient portal requests each follow their own route, and the right one depends on where your client was treated. For personal injury and malpractice firms, a misrouted request or flawed authorization can stall a case early. That's why many firms hand this work to[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) , which checks authorizations, follows up with each facility, and reviews returned records for gaps.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


UPMC offers physician-office, hospital-specific, and MyUPMC request options, so pick the route that matches the treating facility and the requester


-


Pennsylvania's 2026 maximum copying charges, where applicable, are[$2.00 per page](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/health/resources/medical-record-fees) for pages 1 to 20, $1.48 for pages 21 to 60, and $0.52 after that


-


The physician-office Verisma form excludes several Central Pennsylvania locations, but Central PA hospital records can still be requested through MyUPMC, fax, or mail


-


UPMC's posted authorization defaults to 90 days after signature unless another expiration is specified, up to a one-year maximum


-


Incomplete or invalid authorizations can delay processing, so catching errors before submission is one of the simplest ways to keep a request moving


-


Processing time varies by facility, request scope, authorization completeness, and payment requirements, so confirm the expected turnaround with the department handling the request


-


Codes Health advertises an average turnaround of a couple of weeks and pairs flat fee pricing with AI authorization checks and completeness review for law firms


## **Understanding UPMC's Medical Records Request Process**


### **Navigating UPMC's Release of Information Policies**


UPMC provides physician-office, hospital-specific, and MyUPMC request options. Select the route appropriate to the treating facility and the requester.


-


**Physician Office Records** go through UPMC's partnership with Verisma, an online request form covering primary care, specialists, UPMC Children's Community Pediatrics, UPMC Hillman Cancer Center, and UPMC Rehabilitation Institute locations. Check the[UPMC medical records](https://www.upmc.com/patients-visitors/medical-records) page for current access instructions.


-


**Hospital Records** are handled by each facility's medical records department. This covers inpatient admissions, emergency department visits, outpatient surgery, and diagnostic testing. Procedures and contact details vary by hospital, which adds complexity to multi-provider cases.


-


**MyUPMC Requests** let patients submit a formal copy request through the patient portal (steps below).


### **General Guidelines for Submitting a Request**


Before you send anything to UPMC, confirm:


-


The exact facility name where treatment occurred


-


Whether the location is a physician office or a hospital


-


The correct submission route for that location


-


All required form elements, including signatures, dates, and any sensitive-record selections


-


The records you need, whether that's selected categories and date ranges or a complete record


For requests governed by[HIPAA's right of access](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.524) , providers generally must act within 30 calendar days. One additional extension of up to 30 days is permitted if the provider gives the required written explanation and expected completion date before the initial deadline. Don't assume this framework applies identically to every attorney authorization request, and keep in mind that state rules can add their own requirements.


## **Required Forms for Medical Record Release from UPMC**


### **Downloading UPMC-Specific Release Forms**


For routine authorization-based requests, use the current form and instructions for the relevant facility. UPMC posts an[authorization release form](https://dam.upmc.com/-/media/upmc/patients-visitors/medical-records/documents/medical-release-form.pdf?hash=566F6BB2D8C1A54881F4AED2539CD806&rev=36466d139588448db30e735c9bb9026d) alongside its request instructions. Clearly identify the records sought; a request may cover selected categories or a complete record.


**Key Form Elements:**


-


Patient full legal name, date of birth, and current address


-


Accurate patient identifiers, following the receiving department's identity-verification instructions


-


Authorized recipient, including the law firm's name, address, and contact information


-


Records requested, described by category, date range, or as a complete record


-


Purpose of disclosure, such as "legal representation"


-


An unambiguous expiration date or event


-


Patient signature and date


-


Sensitive-record selections, if applicable


### **Ensuring Your HIPAA Authorization is Complete**


Incomplete or invalid authorizations can delay processing. Across medical record retrieval, authorization errors are a leading preventable cause of denied requests. Watch for these common problems:


-


**Missing signatures** : An unsigned form generally can't be processed. The posted form does offer a limited witnessed oral-authorization option for patients who are physically unable to sign.


-


**Unclear expiration** : The posted authorization defaults to 90 days after signature unless another expiration is specified, subject to its one-year maximum. Use an unambiguous expiration.


-


**Identifier discrepancies** : Provide accurate patient identifiers and ask the receiving department how to document name changes or discrepancies.


-


**Unclear record descriptions** : Spell out the categories, date ranges, and facilities you need, or state clearly that you're requesting the complete record.


-


**Sensitive-record selections** : The posted form requires checkboxes for records from licensed mental-health and drug/alcohol facilities. HIV information is included unless its "Do not release" box is checked.


If a deficiency comes up, resolve it with the receiving department and confirm the request's status.


Codes Health's AI review is designed to catch these errors before submission. The system automatically flags misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise lead to provider rejections, so fewer requests bounce back for resubmission.

These details are listed on the[UPMC East records](https://www.upmc.com/locations/hospitals/east/patients-and-visitors/medical-records) page. Verify the appropriate destination before sending another facility's request.

**Physician Office Records:**


-

-


Contact the specific UPMC physician practice with questions about a request


### **Utilizing UPMC's Online Request Options**


For physician-office records, the Verisma form lets you submit the request and upload the authorization online. Follow the instructions displayed in the form, and check with the practice if you're unsure the request went through.


**Central Pennsylvania Note** : The physician-office Verisma form excludes Central Pennsylvania locations, including Harrisburg, Carlisle, Hanover, Lititz, and York. For Central PA hospital records, UPMC also accepts requests through MyUPMC, by fax, or by mail using the contact details above. For excluded physician offices, contact the practice directly for its instructions.


## **How to Request Your Medical Records Online from UPMC**


### **Step-by-Step Guide to MyUPMC Requests**


Patients can request a formal copy of their records through MyUPMC, which makes it a handy option when your client is comfortable using the portal:


1.


Log in to MyUPMC and open the main menu


2.


Select Sharing Hub


3.


Complete the request form


4.


Look for processed documents in Document Center


Walking a client through these steps can get a formal request moving. Patients can also view items like visit summaries and lab results in the portal, which helps with early case assessment. You'll find portal details in the[MyUPMC instructions](https://www.upmc.com/patients-visitors/medical-records) .


### **Troubleshooting Online Access Issues**


Follow the portal's displayed browser and upload instructions. If submission fails or receipt is uncertain, contact the receiving office for assistance. It also helps to save a screenshot of each submission.


## **Obtaining Old or Archived Medical Records from UPMC**


### **UPMC's Policies for Records Retention**


Retention rules depend on who holds the record:


-


**Pennsylvania hospitals** : Records generally must be retained for at least seven years after discharge. Minors' records must be retained through majority and then seven years, or as long as adult records are maintained, under the[hospital retention rule](https://www.pacodeandbulletin.gov/Display/pacode?file=%2Fsecure%2Fpacode%2Fdata%2F028%2Fchapter115%2Fs115.23.html) .


-


**Physician practices** : Physician records governed by 49 Pa. Code § 16.95 generally require seven years after the last documented medical service, extended when necessary through one year after a minor reaches majority.


-


**Archived records** : Older files may take longer to pull from storage.


These are Pennsylvania requirements. Don't assume they govern UPMC facilities in other states.


### **Strategies for Locating Records from Merged Hospitals**


Malpractice and catastrophic injury cases often need records from facilities that changed ownership or joined UPMC. Common challenges include:


-


Closed practices now managed by different UPMC departments


-


Records from pre-merger facility systems that weren't fully integrated


-


Clients who can't recall every treatment location


-


Insurance EOBs and pharmacy records that can point to missing providers


Codes Health uses provider-location tools and missing-record detection to help identify treatment sources and gaps that require follow-up.


## **HIPAA Authorization for Family Members and Third Parties for UPMC Records**


### **Completing a HIPAA Form for a Loved One's Records**


Start by determining who may authorize disclosure for the specific records.


-


**For Deceased Patients:** Confirm the requester's authority under applicable law and UPMC's documentation requirements. The posted[regional authorization form](https://dam.upmc.com/-/media/upmc/campaigns/south-central-pa/documents/patients-visitors/med-records-form.pdf?hash=16533556979C10678AD499EDF77B3E1B&la=en&rev=a5521dc62439461e904764420051a5a6) identifies next of kin with a death certificate and an executor with letters of administration or testamentary. Don't assume a healthcare power of attorney establishes post-death records access.


-


**For Minor Patients:** A parent or guardian typically signs, but certain minor-consented services have different authorization rules. Check who controls access to the specific records before you send the request.


-


**For Incapacitated Adults:** Provide the applicable document establishing the representative's authority, such as guardianship papers or a power of attorney, depending on the situation.


### **Specific UPMC Requirements for Third-Party Requests**


Provide the applicable authorization and any documentation UPMC requests to verify the signer's authority, plus contact information for verification. A retainer agreement or engagement letter doesn't replace a valid authorization.


## **Ensuring Completeness and Accuracy of Retrieved UPMC Records**


### **Verifying All Requested Records Are Included**


Cross-reference delivered records against the original request. Compare billing records to treatment notes, verify every requested date range, confirm requested imaging is included, and check for missing facilities in multi-provider cases.


UPMC directs requesters to the radiology department where testing occurred for imaging. Written radiology reports and the images themselves are different things, so be specific about which you need.


### **What to Do If Records Appear Incomplete**


When records look incomplete:


-


Submit a targeted supplemental request listing the missing dates and services


-


Ask the facility's medical records department to confirm nothing was omitted


-


Use billing codes to find procedures without matching clinical notes


Codes Health checks delivered records against the original request before closing the retrieval process. When records appear incomplete, the team works with the facility to resolve identified gaps before returning the completed set to your firm.


## **Streamlining UPMC Medical Record Retrieval for Legal Cases**


### **Expediting Records for Litigation Deadlines**


Manual retrieval often involves several handoffs. At UPMC East, for example:


1.


Your firm submits the authorization


2.


UPMC East states that an invoice should arrive within 7 to 10 days after it receives the request


3.


Your firm pays the invoice


4.


Records are mailed the day after payment is received


Confirm the process for other facilities, since UPMC In Home publishes a different workflow. Processing time varies by facility, request scope, authorization completeness, and payment requirements, so confirm the expected turnaround with the department handling the request.


A client treated at several UPMC locations may need more than one request route. Confirm which facilities can be covered by one authorization and which require separate submissions. Track each request independently; billing and delivery arrangements may differ.


### **Common Challenges for Legal Professionals**


-


**Multi-Provider Coordination** : UPMC facilities can have different procedures and contacts, which eats into staff time.


-


**Payment Tracking** : Where a facility bills by invoice, a missed invoice can hold up delivery.


-


**Decentralized Contacts** : Department hours and response times vary. Check the relevant facility's current contact information.


### **Pennsylvania Fee Structure for 2026**


Pennsylvania's 2026 maximum copying charges, where applicable, are listed as "Not to Exceed" amounts:


-


**Pages 1 to 20** : $2.00 per page (20 pages = $40.00)


-


**Pages 21 to 60** : $1.48 per page (40 pages = $59.20)


-


**Pages 61 and beyond** : $0.52 per page


**200-page example** : $172.00 in page-copying charges at the stated maximum rates, before other lawful charges


-


Pages 1 to 20: $40.00


-


Pages 21 to 60: $59.20


-


Pages 61 to 200: $72.80


**Other charges that may apply:**


-


Microfilm copies: $2.95 per copy


-


Search and retrieval: $29.61, where allowed (excluded for an individual's own HIPAA access request)


-


Postage and shipping: actual cost


-


Radiology images: handled through the radiology department where testing occurred, with charges that may differ


The fee schedule is published by the[Pennsylvania Department of Health](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/health/resources/medical-record-fees) .


**Patient access versus third-party requests** : For an individual requesting their own records under HIPAA, permitted fees are reasonable and cost-based. They may include copying labor, permitted supplies, requested postage, and an agreed explanation or summary. Search and retrieval charges are excluded, per[HHS fee guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/may-a-covered-entity-charge-individuals-a-fee/index.html) . Don't assume the same federal fee limit applies when records are sent directly to a law firm or another third party.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the average processing time for medical record requests from UPMC?**


It varies by facility, request scope, authorization completeness, and payment requirements. UPMC East, for example, states that an invoice should arrive within 7 to 10 days after it receives the request and that records are mailed the day after payment. For requests under HIPAA's individual right of access, providers generally must act within 30 calendar days, with one possible 30-day extension.


### **Is there a fee for requesting my own medical records from UPMC?**


It can be. For an individual requesting their own records under HIPAA, permitted fees are reasonable and cost-based and may include copying labor, permitted supplies, requested postage, and an agreed explanation or summary. Search and retrieval charges are excluded. Patients can also view many records electronically through MyUPMC.


### **Can I request medical records for a deceased family member from UPMC?**


Yes, if you have the authority to do so. Confirm your authority under applicable law and UPMC's documentation requirements. The posted form identifies next of kin with a death certificate and an executor with letters of administration or testamentary. Don't assume a healthcare power of attorney establishes post-death records access.


### **What should I do if UPMC denies my request for medical records?**


If the issue is an authorization deficiency, resolve it with the receiving department and resubmit. For a denial governed by HIPAA's individual-access rule, review the written denial and any applicable review rights. A suspected HIPAA violation may be raised with the provider or the HHS Office for Civil Rights.


### **How long does UPMC retain medical records?**


It depends on the record holder. Pennsylvania hospitals generally must keep records at least seven years after discharge, with longer periods for minors, while physician records generally must be kept seven years after the last documented service. Request older records as early as possible in case development.


### **Can I request only specific parts of my medical record from UPMC?**


Yes. Your authorization can cover selected categories, such as emergency department records, operative reports, radiology reports or images, and billing records, or a complete record. A narrower request can also reduce page-copying charges.
